The Value of Duck-embryo Vaccine
and High-Egg-Passage Flury Vaccine in Experimental
Rabies Infection in Guinea-pigs
N. VEERARAGHAVAN, M.B.B.S., D.Sc.' & T. P. SUBRAHMANYAN, M.Sc.2
The authors have compared the value of multiple doses ofduck-embryo and HEP Flury
vaccine with that of pooled 5 % sheep-brain vaccine in experimental rabies infection in
guinea-pigs.
They found that the duck-embryo vaccine given in a dosage corresponding
to 14 ml of 10 % vaccine (the dosage recommended for human treatment), either alone
or with antirabies s

summary.text: The opening of a 1963 Bulletin article by Veeraraghavan and Subrahmanyan comparing duck-embryo and HEP Flury rabies vaccines with pooled sheep-brain vaccine in guinea-pigs. The abstract reports that the avian embryo vaccines gave little protection after infection, even at high doses, while pooled phenolized vaccine worked well. It concludes that the recommended human dose of duck-embryo vaccine is inadequate and HEP Flury vaccine is unsuited for post-infection treatment, before reviewing earlier work on the duck-embryo vaccine.

summary.text: Notes agreement with other findings that many duck-embryo vaccine lots fail potency requirements, and judges HEP Flury vaccine too poor for post-infection use. The conclusions restate that the recommended human dose of duck-embryo vaccine is inadequate and that nervous tissue vaccines should be replaced only after careful studies.
